predecessors.name: Kushan Empire
predecessors.text: the western half of the Kushan realm: Bactria, Sogdia and the Kabul valley

successors.name: Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom
successors.text: Bactria, Sogdia, Kabul and Gandhara: the Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom, 'established c.

ledger.x: 226: the western half of the Kushan realm divides from the east.

c. 230: Sasanian governors take over as Kushanshahs. 'The Sasanian Empire captured the provinces of Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara from the declining Kushan Empire' in 225 and 'extended their dominion into Bactria during the reign of Ardashir I around 230'; 'the local Sasanian governors then went on to take the title of…

c. 230: the Kushanshah kingdom is a Sasanian dependency. Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom page (re-read 2026-10-19): 'The Sasanian Empire captured the provinces of Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara from the declining Kushan Empire' (following a series of wars in 225 CE); 'The Sassanids... extended their dominion into Bactria…
259: the Kushanshah kingdom continues as the Kushano-Sasanian (Indo-Sasanian) Kingdom.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of the Kushan lands
wars.outcome: The Sasanians captured Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara, installed Kushanshah governors and extended to western Pakistan under Shapur I (240-270).

certainty.note: The Bactrian, Kabul and Gandharan limits are inferred from mints and inscriptions, not from lines; the Sasanian frontier with the Eastern Kushans at the Indus is approximate.
